build: two pre-release Andrey builds: the standardized grid on the 0.12.0 build (29 October 2026), the unstandardized and d = 200 grids on the 0.13.0 build (30 October 2026)

regimes.linear_gauss_er: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, standardized, d 20/50/100, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4; seeds 0-19 attempted, at least 10 per setting run
regimes.linear_gauss_er_unitless: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, not standardized; d 20/50/100, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4; seeds 0-19 attempted, 10 to 16 run (CPU budget guard)
regimes.linear_gauss_er_d200: linear-Gaussian Erdos-Renyi graphs, standardized, d 200, n 1000/5000, mean degree 2/4, the blanket methods whose d=100 fits all finished; seeds 0-9

verdict_rule: D = error(Andrey) - error(bnlearn) per dataset on the datasets both finished; a setting with at least 10 paired datasets is worse when the paired 95% percentile-bootstrap interval of the mean D lies entirely above 0, better when entirely below, a tie otherwise; fewer than 10 pairs is reported, not judged; a setting that is worse is rerun once on fresh seeds (a replication, in the row) and counts as worse only if the rerun's own interval also lies entirely above 0
fit_protocol: one fit at a time on 1 core, Fisher-z tests at alpha 0.05 (bnlearn test zf), a 600 s wall cap per fit, 1 untimed warm-up fit except at n=5000, mean degree 4, d>=50 (none), 1 timed fit; a capped fit is a timeout, counted as coverage and never scored
error_metric: each entry's own, in its error_metric: the SHD of the output against its own true graph (the moral graph, the skeleton, or the CPDAG), as the median over the paired datasets (the _mean fields hold the means)
complete_definition: true when every setting has at least 10 paired datasets (both packages finished); a setting with fewer is listed in incomplete, its timeouts counted in the timeout columns and never scored
seeds_note: seeds is the number of datasets attempted per setting: 10 to 20 of the 20 planned in the standardized grid, 10 to 16 of 20 in the unstandardized grid (the CPU budget guard skipped the rest before they ran), and 10 of 10 at 200 variables

methods.note: The setting with 50 variables, 5,000 rows, and mean degree 2 is worse (D +0.50 [+0.05, +1.05]); 16 of its 20 graphs are identical. Most of the gap, +7 pairs of the +10 over its 20 datasets, sits in 2 datasets whose skeletons differ, and the skeleton difference starts at one node's first grow step, where the p-values of several candidates underflow to exactly 0 in bnlearn, which takes the first column among them. Andrey takes the candidate with the strongest test statistic, the association measure of Tsamardinos, Aliferis, and Statnikov (2003). bnlearn's choice, applied in Andrey's search, reproduces bnlearn's skeleton in all 4 traced datasets. The other +3 are orientation differences in 2 datasets with equal skeletons: Meek's rules on a cyclic partially directed graph, and a collider that bnlearn skips for closing a directed cycle.
